text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--Danish scientists report progress in experiments to clone an adult cow at Foulum Embryo-Technology Centre in west Denmark. A hearing on cloning was scheduled to take place in parliamemt Wednesday.

--Lower admission fees, new entertainments including a children's play area and more late night pop for the young are the main elements in the new strategy to bring Copenhagen's Tivoli Gardens back into the black after two years of deficit with falling visitors and revenue.
--Swedish economic expert proposes establishing a monetary union in the Nordic region with common currency.

--Rumours circulate in parliament about a possible premature autumn general election in Denmark in September in connection with the unveiling of the 1998 draft state budget in late August. Sources in the prime minister's office say the latest opinion polls indicate it would not be to the Social Democratic minority government's advantage to wait until its full term in office ends in September 1998.

--Former Danish Central Bank governor Erik Hoffmeyer, now chairman of the board of Copenhagen Stock Exchange, says the bourse may be forced to give up its opposition to issuing share and bond data on Internet, saying he intends to bring the matter up at a coming board meeting.
--Competition between Danish and Swedish brokers is expected to become more fierce as a result of a new cooperation pact between Copenhagen and Stockholm stock exchanges.
